mbm-0243.clue: I have a ribbon for taking my time.
mbm-0243.quote: I entered the corn-on-the-cob contest with braces fresh off my teeth. The judge said I’d left the cleanest cob she’d ever seen and made me a ribbon from a napkin. It’s in a frame.

mbm-0244.clue: The smallest part has four footprints.
mbm-0244.quote: A ladybug walked across the wet paint on my model rover. I let the marks dry and painted a little flag beside them. Our model club voted it evidence of life.

mbm-0245.clue: I always visit the mended plate.
mbm-0245.quote: There’s a plate in the museum with a neat row of metal staples across a crack. Somebody loved it enough to stitch a dish. I look at it every time I’m tempted to throw something away.

mbm-0246.clue: The red fish is hanging by one whisker.
mbm-0246.quote: I cut a paper catfish for my sister’s window. The paper curled in the damp and its whisker lifted off the glass. In the morning light it looks as if it’s testing the water.

mbm-0247.clue: My first set came in a cocoa tin.
mbm-0247.quote: The dominoes rattled so much when I carried them to the neighbors that our dog learned the sound. Now he beats me to their front step and claims the chair by the fan.

mbm-0248.clue: The medal is still in the laundry basket.
mbm-0248.quote: I entered a forms exhibition in a borrowed uniform. Its owner tucked a note inside the sash that said breathe. I gave the uniform back freshly washed and slipped my medal in with the note.

mbm-0249.clue: I sewed the pink square twice.
mbm-0249.quote: My niece insisted her doll should have the same quilt as her bed. There wasn’t enough pink for another square. We shared the corner of an old hair ribbon and both quilts have a bow.

mbm-0250.clue: I throw from the kitchen chalk line.
mbm-0250.quote: The longest Frisbee throw I’ve ever made went in through an open back door and landed on a cooling rack. My neighbor served it back to me beside the biscuits.

mbm-0251.quote: My first job started before dawn, so I saved scraps the colors of the sky at each bus stop. At picnics my spouse traces the whole ride along the red checks, from charcoal at the hem to pale peach.

mbm-0252.clue: I named the hold after a dumpling.
mbm-0252.quote: One climbing hold feels exactly like the pleated edge of my aunt’s dumplings. It’s where I pause for a breath. Everyone at the gym calls it the lunch break now.

mbm-0253.clue: Those chalk flowers are mile markers.
mbm-0253.quote: My little cousin came along on a bike and drew a flower each time I finished a lap. After the shower came through, I found one pink petal still sheltered under the bench.

mbm-0254.quote: I practiced a vallenato tune with a strip of ribbon tied to my accordion. On the long note it floated straight out. My aunt caught the ribbon and danced the last verse beside me.

mbm-0255.clue: I borrow my uncle’s empty shop.
mbm-0255.quote: The shutters on his barber shop are metal. When I sing after closing I get a little chorus for free. The shaving brushes make an unusually tidy audience.

mbm-0256.clue: My juggling lesson starts under the table.
mbm-0256.quote: I gave my nephew three silk scarves. He lay on the rug and watched them float above him before he tried a single catch. Now whenever I drop one, he tells me the view is better down there.

mbm-0257.clue: My paint rag has a very steady horizon.
mbm-0257.quote: I wiped a brush on a cloth at the same spot every day for a week. By Friday it looked like an evening seascape. I clipped it to the easel and gave the actual canvas a rest.

mbm-0258.clue: I built my first antenna under the kitchen table.
mbm-0258.quote: We stretched the wire along the old curtain rail. The first station I heard had rain slapping the window behind the operator. Our kitchen was bone dry. I remember that better than his call sign.

mbm-0259.clue: I save the last run for the trees.
mbm-0259.quote: There’s an easy slope through a little stand of pine. I take it slowly on the way home so I can hear the hiss change when the needles turn to snow under my skis.

mbm-0260.clue: The mitten tree has my brother’s striped one.
mbm-0260.quote: We skied past a row of lost things hanging outside the lodge. My brother recognized his old mitten from the chairlift. It took us two runs to collect it because we were laughing so hard.

mbm-0261.clue: I paid a coin for the sound.
mbm-0261.quote: I picked up a chipped blue vase at the market and tapped it. It rang like the tram bell by my old house. I spent my last coin and rang it very gently all the way home.

mbm-0262.clue: Everybody wants the one with the extra edge.
mbm-0262.quote: My little niece pressed an arepa with the bottom of a mug and left a funny lip around it. It crisped up beautifully. Her mug has been promoted to kitchen equipment.

mbm-0263.clue: My beard comes off on cue.
mbm-0263.quote: I play two old sailors in the same show. One beard sticks on with a little hook. The other sailor has to come on holding a handkerchief because his chin itches where the hook was.

mbm-0264.clue: Our set opens with a key turning.
mbm-0264.quote: Our practice room door squeaks a perfect note. We recorded it on a cassette, and that creak is the first sound in our set. My landlady can recognize us from the hall.

mbm-0265.clue: There’s a little door under the castle.
mbm-0265.quote: At mini golf the ball vanished behind the ramp. The owner opened a tiny wooden door and found four red balls and a toy soldier. We left him there to guard the next round.

mbm-0266.clue: I follow the shadow of the lift.
mbm-0266.quote: Just before closing, the lift chairs cast long blue shadows down the snow. I like making easy turns between them. Empty chairs don’t mind how slowly I go.

mbm-0267.clue: The spoon drawer lost its lining.
mbm-0267.quote: I used a strip from the old kitchen drawer to border my quilt. It still has a faint outline where the teaspoons lay. I added silver stitches and gave every one a handle.
